messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

function.name: genetics_get_variant_frequency

message.content: The most well‑documented “dominant” genetic trait in lions is the presence of a mane in adult males. In lion populations, the allele that codes for a full mane is inherited in a dominant fashion: a male that carries just one copy of the mane allele will develop a mane, whereas a female (or a male that is homozygous recessive) will not. This trait is strongly linked to the Y‑linked gene that controls the development of the mane, making it a classic example of a dominant genetic feature in lions.
